data.narrative:
Fleet Space Technologies, a Series C space and aerospace company that has raised $70M+, was valued using two applicable triangulation methods against a peer set of 6 private-stage comparables in the sector (with an additional 5 public anchors for reference). The peer universe spans Sierra Space ($8.0B, Series C), Apex Space ($2.3B, Series D), Cowboy Space Corporation ($2.0B, Series B), Varda Space Industries ($1.6B, Series D), and Aalyria ($1.3B, Series B), yielding a median valuation of $1.8B and a range of $1.1B to $8.0B.

The stage-progression method applied a 1.7x multiplier to the $70M total raised proxy, implying $119M. The peer-median method directly referenced the 6-company cohort, implying $1.8B. A public-comp anchoring approach using 27.4x P/S across 5 traded aerospace peers (RKLB, PL, LUNR, ASTS, SATL) could not be applied due to absence of target revenue disclosure.

Triangulation across the two applicable methods supports a valuation range of $101M (low) to $2.1B (high), with a median of $954M. The substantial spread reflects fundamental uncertainty in comparable selection and stage-specific risk in early-stage space ventures. Key uncertainties include revenue trajectory, unit economics, and execution risk relative to the heterogeneous peer set.
